proposals.evidence: Full ma explicitly explains the replacement of old aham by the oblique/instrumental pronoun (Prakrit maē, Apabhramsha maï̃), listing Assamese maï, Bengali mui, Oriya mu/mũ and Punjabi/Lahnda maĩ/mɛ̃. These whole first-person singular responses match those regional nominative continuations, preserving length, nasalization and source vowel notation. They are not assigned to aham merely from their nominative function; accusative molā and additional case endings are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Full nava lists Oriya nūā/lūā and western Gujarati navũ, Marathi navā and Hindi nawā, with Prakrit ṇa(v)a. These vowel/glide and v/b forms retain the corresponding plain new-adjective stem; source dot and nasalization notation are preserved. This is a regional family link, leaving contact open; forms with a lexical l/n extension and ambiguous short nai are excluded.

proposals.evidence: Section 1 chagala includes Oriya cheḷi and Bihari/Hindi cherī “goat”, in the same chēla family. These eastern survey ceṛi/ceḍī responses match that feminine goat series with loss or variation of aspiration and the source’s retroflex/flap notation retained. The link leaves contact across neighboring eastern languages open.
